- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

p## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that

walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

.## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

U## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

n## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

 ## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

  what it would do anyway

- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and

alone and the *target* moves.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

alone and the *target* moves.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

b## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

a## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

  what it would do anyway

- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own

s## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

alone and the *target* moves.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

p## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

M## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

,## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

alone and the *target* moves.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

s## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

t## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

### Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

 ## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own

walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

m## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.

s## Puppet mode

Taking control makes Hornet an **invisible lure** and leaves the enemy running its own AI.

- **Left-click** anywhere to move her. The enemy walks over and attacks, because that is
  what it would do anyway
- **Right-click** to select a different enemy
- Hornet is **invulnerable**, **invisible**, and **cannot act** — no needle, no movement
- The camera follows the enemy

### Why the lure, instead of steering

Both earlier attempts fought the creature rather than using it. Writing velocity produced
something gliding around under an idle animation. Firing movement states was better but
still guesswork about which state meant "walk" — the Moss Spitter kept picking its jump.

Enemies already know how to approach Hornet; that is most of what their FSMs do. Letting
them do it gets the right gait, the right approach distance, the right attack spacing and
the right animations — none of which a puppeteer fakes convincingly. So the enemy is left
alone and the *target* moves.

This also means Override suppression is switched **off** during puppet mode. The claim is
still held so attacks can be fired by hand, but suppressing the enemy's decisions would
stop it noticing or approaching the lure, which is the entire mechanism.

### Hornet is hidden, not removed

Her renderers are disabled and her input is blocked through the game's own
`AddInputBlocker`. She stays physically present on purpose — enemies target her, and that
targeting is exactly what is being used. An earlier version moved her to the *Ignore
Raycast* layer to stop enemies seeing her, which also removed terrain collision and dropped
her out of the world.

She is made kinematic and re-pinned every frame, since knockback, conveyors and enemies
walking into her would otherwise drag the lure around mid-fight.

### Enemies that ignore Hornet

Fall back to arrow keys firing the enemy's own movement states, and the UI says so. An
enemy with no targeting behaviour has nothing for the lure to work on.
